findings.title: Multiple execSync calls should use security wrapper
findings.description: The dashboard server uses execSync in multiple locations. While security utilities exist, not all calls use the safeExec wrapper.
findings.recommendation: Audit all execSync/spawn calls and migrate to use the safeExec wrapper from utils/security.js for consistent sanitization

findings.title: Example credentials in documentation
findings.description: Documentation files contain example API keys and credentials. While these are placeholders, it sets a pattern that could lead to accidental credential exposure.
findings.recommendation: Replace example credentials with obviously fake values like 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE' or use environment variable references

findings.title: Trust proxy enabled
findings.description: The server has 'trust proxy' enabled. This is appropriate if behind a reverse proxy but could be a concern if deployed directly.
findings.recommendation: Ensure this setting matches your deployment topology. Document the expected deployment configuration.

findings.title: CSP disabled for dashboard
findings.description: Content Security Policy is disabled (contentSecurityPolicy: false) to allow inline scripts for the dashboard.
findings.recommendation: Consider implementing a tailored CSP policy that allows necessary inline scripts while blocking dangerous patterns
